# Without an option, wc writes every number.
$ printf 'one two\nthree four\nfive\n' | wc
3 5 24
[exit 0]

# The flag --words selects the number of words.
$ printf 'one two\nthree four\nfive\n' | wc --words
5
[exit 0]

# Short flags combine in one argument.
$ printf 'one two\nthree four\nfive\n' | wc -lc
3 24
[exit 0]

# An empty standard input has no lines.
$ wc --lines
0
[exit 0]

# An unknown flag fails with the exit status 2.
$ printf 'one two\nthree four\nfive\n' | wc --chars
wc: unknown flag --chars
[exit 2]

# A failed write fails with the exit status 1.
$ printf 'one two\nthree four\nfive\n' | wc >/dev/full
wc: main: write the numbers: clitest: no space left on device
[exit 1]

# A failed read fails with the exit status 1.
$ wc <&-
wc: main: read the standard input: clitest: bad file descriptor
[exit 1]
